questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Construct the line through P parallel to line ℓ.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.
Construct the line through P parallel to line ℓ.
questions.correct_answer: Draw a transversal through P meeting ℓ at A; copy the angle it makes with ℓ at A to P in the corresponding position; the new side is parallel to ℓ.

questions.skill: Justify the parallel-line constructions
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: To construct a line through P parallel to ℓ, a transversal through P meets ℓ at A, and the angle at A is copied at P in the corresponding position. Prove that the new line is parallel to ℓ.
questions.prompt_markup: To construct a line through P parallel to ℓ, a transversal through P meets ℓ at A, and the angle at A is copied at P in the corresponding position. Prove that the new line is parallel to ℓ.
questions.required_method: Use the congruence of the copied angle (SSS) and the converse of the corresponding angles theorem.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof. Essential: the copy is congruent (SSS from the construction); the angles are corresponding angles along AP; the converse gives parallel lines.

questions.response: write the answer and show the required work
questions.prompt: In the two-perpendicular construction, k ⊥ ℓ and n ⊥ k at P. Prove that n ∥ ℓ.
questions.prompt_markup: In the two-perpendicular construction, k ⊥ ℓ and n ⊥ k at P. Prove that n ∥ ℓ.
questions.required_method: Both n and ℓ make right angles with k (corresponding angles congruent), or two lines perpendicular to the same line in a plane are parallel.
questions.grading_note: Any valid proof (paragraph, two-column, or flow). Essential: n ⊥ k and ℓ ⊥ k give a pair of congruent (90°) corresponding angles where k crosses n and ℓ; congruent corresponding angles give n ∥ ℓ. Alternative: two lines perpendicular to the same line are parallel (with that theorem cited). Invalid: "they look parallel".

questions.skill: Divide a segment into equal parts with parallel lines
questions.standard_level: Geometry. Common Core groups high-school standards by category, not by course; this bank places this one in Geometry, following the Common Core traditional pathway (Appendix A) except where engine/hs_courses.py says otherwise.
questions.prompt: Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs. Divide segment AB into three congruent parts.
questions.prompt_markup:
Compass and straightedge only; leave all arcs.
Divide segment AB into three congruent parts.
questions.correct_answer: Draw a ray from A; mark three equal steps C, D, E on it with the compass; join E to B; construct parallels to EB through D and C; they cut AB into three equal parts.
questions.grading_note: Grade the construction marks, not only the final figure: three equal compass steps on the auxiliary ray and two parallel constructions.

questions.prompt: To divide AB into three equal parts, three equal steps are marked on a ray from A, the last mark is joined to B, and parallels to that segment are drawn through the other marks. Why do the parallel lines divide AB into equal parts?
questions.prompt_markup: To divide AB into three equal parts, three equal steps are marked on a ray from A, the last mark is joined to B, and parallels to that segment are drawn through the other marks. Why do the parallel lines divide AB into equal parts?
questions.correct_answer: Parallel lines cut the two sides of the triangle proportionally (triangle proportionality), so equal steps on the ray give equal parts of AB.
